q: The Vitali-Carathéodory theorem states that every integrable function f can be approximated by functions of the form l ≤ f ≤ u where l is upper semi-continuous and u is lower semi-continuous with:
exp: Vitali-Carathéodory: for f ∈ L¹, and any ε > 0, ∃ upper semi-continuous l ≤ f and lower semi-continuous u ≥ f with ∫(u−l)dx < ε. This gives 'semi-continuous envelopes' approximating f, used in capacity theory and potential analysis.
